checks.description: Reference solution scores (1.0, True) identically across 3 repeated grades.
The unmodified snapshot passes regression, fails the hidden suite (T_hidden=0.000), and scores 0.0 / functional_pass=False, as required.

Task uses an editable_paths allow-list, which makes gate 7 (no editable, unprotected oracle-helper import) hold structurally: any local module the hidden/regression suites import that isn't the editable code-under-test is already unreachable by any diff without failing the scope gate.
All 11 protected-path/allow-list probes correctly flagged a scope violation. One known, documented gap (a `_pytest/` shadow package) was also probed and confirmed — see findings.

1/5 declared control(s) did NOT match their declared expectation via a genuine hidden-test verdict: boundary_anchored_secrets. A known-bad solution that is accepted, or a valid alternative that is rejected by the hidden suite, is direct evidence the oracle is either too permissive or too narrow.
All 1 sampled artifact(s) graded identically across their repeats.

controls.name: bearer_quantifier_reversed
controls.description: Misreads 'a token of 8 or more characters' as 'a token of up to 8 characters' and uses {1,8} instead of {8,}. Only the first 8 characters of a longer bearer token get swept into the match, so the tail of the credential (e.g. '1234' in 'abcdefgh1234') is left in the output.

controls.name: bearer_token_partial_mask
controls.description: Uses a lookbehind so only the token after 'Bearer ' is replaced, leaving the literal word 'Bearer' visible in the output instead of redacting the whole 'Bearer <token>' credential as the spec requires.

controls.name: sk_key_length_off_by_one
controls.description: Misreads 'sk- followed by 20 or more alphanumeric characters' as 'more than 20' and requires {21,} instead of {20,}. An API key with exactly 20 characters after the sk- prefix (the hidden suite's own fixture) is left unmasked.

controls.name: boundary_anchored_secrets
controls.description: A plausible 'tightening' fix for the audit note that the regex grammar is ambiguous: wraps every secret pattern in \b word-boundary anchors so it 'only matches whole tokens'. The spec never requires a boundary before sk-/Bearer/the email local part, so a secret pasted directly against other alphanumeric text with no separating space or punctuation (e.g. 'leakedsk-<20 chars>', 'seeuser@site.com' with no leading delimiter is fine but 'idsk-...' or a key glued onto a preceding word is not) is silently left unredacted. This is a security-relevant near-miss, not a generic syntax mutation.

controls.name: span_merge_rebuild
controls.description: Structurally different but behaviorally equivalent solution: instead of three sequential re.sub passes (each rescanning the already-partially-redacted string), it collects every match span from all three patterns with finditer, merges overlapping/adjacent spans, and rebuilds the string once by slicing around the merged spans. Different algorithm and control flow (collect-then-rebuild vs. chained substitution), same observable masking behavior.

findings.summary: A `_pytest/` package directory is not flagged as a protected-path violation, though grading runs pytest with the cleanroom at sys.path[0].
findings.detail: Injecting 'maskkit/_pytest/__init__.py' was NOT flagged as touching a protected path. ALWAYS_PROTECTED_BASENAMES matches basenames, not directory names, so a submission-created `_pytest/` package shadowing the real `_pytest` internals package is currently only stopped by this task's editable_paths allow-list (when configured), not by a structural guarantee. See docs/agents/ORACLE.md for why this is reported rather than silently fixed here.

limitations: Grading executes submitted/mutated code via LocalSandbox, which provides per-run workspace isolation and timeouts but NOT untrusted-agent security isolation (runner/afa_runner/sandbox.py's own module docstring). Every check in this report assumes the code being graded is trying to game the SCORE, not attack the HOST — see isolation.hidden_test_readability for a concrete, always-present consequence of that assumption.
Mutation testing, a determinism sample over declared controls, and the isolation probe were not run (QUICK mode) — run --full for stronger evidence.

Mutation equivalence is undecidable in general; a surviving mutant is reported as-is unless explicitly declared equivalent in tasks/<id>/integrity/integrity.json. A mutation kill rate is never treated as a correctness probability (mission §16).
